notes: The helper net_edge_pct (screen.py ~154-182) uses the same formula as the reference _net_edge_pct: target_bid = vwap*bid_walk/close, then sell_proceeds(maker=False)/ask_walk - 1. It states the shape-preserving assumption in the docstring and at the call site (~348-356), and it is wired into Candidate.net_edge_pct (~381). The 4 hidden reference tests fail only with an ImportError on the private name _net_edge_pct. The brief never named the helper, and the maths is identical, so those tests would pass under that name. The reference also rewrote the below_breakeven gate to net_edge <= min_net_edge_pct, which the brief's 'don't touch the other gates' arguably forbids. The candidate kept the old gate and argued correctly that expected_move > breakeven is algebraically the same as net_edge > 0, so nothing is lost unless min_net_edge_pct is non-zero. The tests are strong: flat book nets exactly -tax to 1e-12, plus an exact fixed-point end-to-end scenario (test_screen_digest.py ~187-225) whose ranking flips under the old formula. The self-review checked this by reverting the change and re-derived the numbers. Trading risk: the change only affects ranking and matches the merged formula, and no order sizing is touched.
